answer: Shards are assigned from the mesa graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The inlet assignment is published and anchor records each panel. The grading quorum of 9 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so an adversary cannot sit on the panel that judges it. A farm of 1210 identities would post 2330 proofs and burn roughly 41 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
